note: Archetypes for simulated screen tests (think-aloud on screenshots). Grounded in docs/48 sections 4-5; each is a hypothesis to recruit real people against, not a finding. Health details are limited to what a person might say about themselves; the site makes no health claims.

personas.profile: Rosa, 68, retired primary-school teacher in Lima (Surco). Sings alto in her parish choir and with her grandchildren. Android phone with the font size turned up; uses WhatsApp, YouTube and Yape every day, online banking only with her son's help. Her voice tires sooner than it used to and she notices she goes flat on long notes. Wary of anything that asks for a card. Expects to be addressed politely and dislikes being called 'adulto mayor'.

Jorge, 59, accountant in Arequipa. Gives monthly reports to the board of his cooperative and speaks at his neighbourhood association; people tell him he mumbles and speaks too fast. Uses a laptop at work, a phone otherwise. Skeptical of apps that promise a lot; would pay for something that works but hates subscriptions he forgets to cancel.

Carmen, 63, homemaker in Madrid. Loves karaoke at family parties and sings along to coplas and Rocío Jurado; was told as a girl at school to just move her lips. Uses an iPhone for WhatsApp, Instagram and online shopping. Careful with money; pays in euros and would look for the price first.

Margaret, 72, retired nurse in Manchester. Sings in a community choir; mild hearing loss in one ear, wears reading glasses. Uses an iPad and a phone; reads the Guardian online, pays for a few subscriptions by card and knows how to cancel them. Wants her voice to stay strong and is put off by anything that talks down to her or calls her a senior.

Valeria, 20, psychology student in Lima (San Miguel). Sings covers in her room and wants to post one on TikTok; goes to karaoke with friends on Fridays. Budget is tight: pays for Spotify Student with Yape and nothing else. Distrusts apps that hide the price or flood her with ads; likes things that feel modern and honest.

Diego, 26, works in sales in Mexico City. Has job interviews coming and presents to clients; his voice shakes when he is nervous and he says 'este...' a lot. Uses his phone for everything; already pays for Netflix and a gym. Has never thought of himself as someone who sings.

Aisha, 23, graduate trainee in Lagos. Sings in her church choir and wants to lead a song; mobile data is expensive and her Android phone is mid-range. Pays with a local card and is careful with anything priced in dollars.

Tom, 31, office job in Chicago. Believes he is tone-deaf; his best friend asked him to sing at the wedding in four months. Uses a laptop at home. Would pay for something that actually works, but has quit two apps after a week.

Lucía, 41, secondary-school teacher in Bogotá. Talks all day in class and her voice is often tired by Friday; would like to project without shouting and also sings with her daughter. Uses her phone; little free time, so anything has to fit in a few minutes.
